main_body: Tall brick townhouse with a slate mansard roof, a dormer and a chimney, an orange cornice, three storeys of windows, a balcony and a green door
top_band: Down the middle column: rows ~10-24 are a grey-teal flat roof panel with a dark frame, rows ~26-42 are blue-grey slate roof slope (the lightest tones at the top), and rows ~42-46 are an orange cornice band at the front edge
evidence: The roof is drawn as a real surface. The flat roof panel and the slate slope with its dormer sit above the wall and read as a horizontal or sloped surface seen from above. The orange cornice is a distinct front-edge line, with a dark shadow row under it before the brick facade starts. The brick wall is a vertical face. Its windows have stone frames and sills and the door sits in an inset surround, so they read as set into the wall. The structure matches the reference houses, which also have a visible roof above a flat wall, so it passes as 3/4.

style.evidence: The brick has several red-brown tones, with per-brick highlights and mortar variation. The slate roof has 4-5 blue-grey steps and scalloped tile rows. The stone window frames have light and shadow edges, and the windows have lit and unlit panes with mullions. The outlines are dark blue-brown tinted to the neighbouring material rather than pure black. Tile density is as high as the references or higher, with no large flat fills.
